items.basis: The proposed mechanism incorrectly assumes droplet-membrane interaction dominates fouling when evidence shows that cake layer formation and pore blocking are the primary fouling mechanisms in submerged MBRs, as demonstrated in doi:10.1016/j.memsci.2007.06.026 which identifies colloidal and particulate matter as the main foulants.

The candidate fails to address the boundary condition of mixed liquor suspended solids at 8 g/L, which creates a high fouling potential that surface hydrophilization alone cannot overcome, as evidenced by doi:10.30684/etj.30.19.14 showing that at MLSS >6 g/L, hydrophilic membranes still experience severe fouling.

The candidate's prediction of 20% flux increase directly contradicts the evidence in doi:10.3390/membranes13030300 which shows that surface modifications typically yield only 5-10% flux improvements in comparable MBR systems.

The claimed novel design variable of membrane surface hydrophilization cannot be implemented without compromising selectivity, as stated in the candidate's own known failure modes, creating an irreconcilable tradeoff between flux and rejection efficiency.

The testable prediction of 20% flux increase is ambiguous regarding the measurement methodology, failing to specify whether this is initial flux, steady-state flux, or flux after a specific fouling period, making validation difficult.
